q-97598.name: Question 1
q-97598.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
q-97598.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\cdot ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+0-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\  & =0, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨sin⁡t,2,cos⁡t⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
0
b
sin⁡2t
c
sin⁡2t+4
d
1
e
sin⁡tcos⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: a=⟨ddt(sin⁡t),ddt(2),ddt(cos⁡t)⟩=⟨cos⁡t,0,−sin⁡t⟩

Next, we compute v⋅a and ||v||: v⋅a=⟨sin⁡t,2,cos⁡t⟩⋅⟨cos⁡t,0,−sin⁡t⟩=sin⁡tcos⁡t+0−cos⁡tsin⁡t,=0,||v||=(sin⁡t)2+(2)2+(cos⁡t)2=sin2⁡t+cos2⁡t+4=1+4=5

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=05=0.

q-97603.name: Question 2
q-97603.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}t,\,{t}^{2},\,t+1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
q-97603.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,2t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,2t,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{(2t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{4t}{2\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-96925.name: Question 3
q-96925.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
q-96925.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{-2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩\cdot ⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩ \\  & ={e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(2{e}^{-2t})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨et,−2e−2t,1⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
 et−8e−2te2t+4e−4t
b
 e2t−8e−4te2t+4e−4t+1
c
 e2t−e−2te2t+e−2t
d
et−2e−2tet+2e−2t+1
e
 et+e−2tet+1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: a=⟨ddt(et),ddt(−2e−2t),ddt(1)⟩=⟨et,4e−2t,0⟩

Next, we compute v⋅a and ||v||:

v⋅a=⟨et,−2e−2t,1⟩⋅⟨et,4e−2t,0⟩=e2t−8e−4t,||v||=(et)2+(2e−2t)2+12=e2t+4e−4t+1.

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=e2t−8e−4te2t+4e−4t+1.

q-97597.name: Question 4
q-97597.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,1,\,3t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
q-97597.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,0,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{t}^{2},\,1,\,3t⟩\cdot ⟨2t,\,0,\,3⟩ \\  & =2{t}^{3}+9t \\  & =t(2{t}^{2}+9), \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({t}^{2})}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+{(3t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{4}+9{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{t(2{t}^{2}+9)}{\sqrt{{t}^{4}+9{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

a
2tt4+9t2+1
b
t(2t2+9)t4+9t2+1
c
tt2+3
d
t2+3t4+9t2+1
e
2t+1t2+3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: a=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(1),ddt(3t)⟩=⟨2t,0,3⟩

Next, we compute v⋅a and ||v||: v⋅a=⟨t2,1,3t⟩⋅⟨2t,0,3⟩=2t3+9t=t(2t2+9),||v||=(t2)2+(1)2+(3t)2=t4+9t2+1

q-97596.name: Question 5
q-97596.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\sqrt{6t},\,3,\,-t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
q-97596.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{6t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{\sqrt{6t}},\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\sqrt{6t},\,3,\,-t⟩\cdot ⟨\frac{3}{\sqrt{6t}},\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =t+3, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{6t})}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}+{(-t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}+6t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{(t+3)^{2}} \\  & =t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{t+3}{t+3} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97613.name: Question 6
q-97613.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{t}^{3}},\,4t,\,-7⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
q-97613.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{t}^{3}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-7)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,4,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨\sqrt{t},\,4,\,0⟩\times ⟨\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}},\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \sqrt{t} & 4 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t} & 4 \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,-\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{t+16}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}})}{\sqrt{t+16}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{t(t+16)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-96928.name: Question 7
q-96928.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
q-96928.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨(-{cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t),-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{2} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

b
cos⁡tsin⁡t+cos⁡t
c

1

sin⁡tcos⁡t

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(1),ddt(cos⁡t),ddt(−sin⁡t)⟩=⟨0,−sin⁡t,−cos⁡t⟩.

Now, we compute v×a,||v|| and ||v×a||:

v×a=⟨1,cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩×⟨0,−sin⁡t,−cos⁡t⟩=ijk1cos⁡t−sin⁡t0−sin⁡t−cos⁡t= cos⁡t−sin⁡t−sin⁡t−cos⁡ti−1−sin⁡t0−cos⁡tj+1cos⁡t0−sin⁡tk=⟨(−cos2⁡t−sin2⁡t),−(−cos⁡t),(−sin⁡t)⟩=⟨−1,cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩||v||=12+(cos⁡t)2+(−sin⁡t)2=1+cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t=2||v×a||=(−1)2+(cos⁡t)2+(−sin⁡t)2=1+cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t=2.

q-97611.name: Question 8
q-97611.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t,\,1,\,\sqrt{2t}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
q-97611.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨t,\,1,\,\sqrt{2t}⟩\times ⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ t & 1 & \sqrt{2t} \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2t} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}t & \sqrt{2t} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}t & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}},\frac{\sqrt{2t}}{2},-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+1}, \\  & =\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}} \\  & =t+1, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}})}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2t}}{2})}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{2t}+\frac{t}{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+2t+1}{2t}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{(t+1)^{2}}{2t}} \\  & =\frac{t+1}{\sqrt{2t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{t+1}{\sqrt{2t}})}{t+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute v×a:

q-97607.name: Question 9
q-97607.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
q-97607.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{1+9} \\  & =\sqrt{10}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9+1} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

q-97609.name: Question 10
q-97609.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨0,\,t,\,2{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
q-97609.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨0,\,t,\,2{t}^{2}⟩\times ⟨0,\,1,\,4t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & t & 2{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 4t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}t & 2{t}^{2} \\ 1 & 4t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2{t}^{2} \\ 0 & 4t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & t \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2},0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(t)}^{2}+{(2{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}+{t}^{2}}, \\  & =t\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(2{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97772.name: Question 11
q-97772.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨-{t}^{2},\,1,\,t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
q-97772.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(1):$

$$
v(1)=⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,0,\,1⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨-2,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\times a(1),||v(1)||,$ and $||v(1)\times a(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\times a(1) & =⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩\times ⟨-2,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}, \\ ||v(1)\times a(1)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(1)\times a(1)||}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $\sqrt{2}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||.

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at t=1, as follows: a=⟨ddt(−t2),ddt(1),ddt(t)⟩=⟨−2t,0,1⟩,a(1)=⟨−2,0,1⟩

Then, we compute v(1)×a(1),||v(1)||, and ||v(1)×a(1)||:

v(1)×a(1)=⟨−1,1,1⟩×⟨−2,0,1⟩=ijk−111−201=1101i−−11−21j+−11−20k=⟨1,−1,2⟩,||v(1)||=(−1)2+12+12=3,||v(1)×a(1)||=12+(−1)2+22=6

q-97765.name: Question 12
q-97765.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨-t,\,1,\,{t}^{2}⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
q-97765.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2t⟩, \\ v(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,2⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨0,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\cdot a(1)$ and $||v(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\cdot a(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,2⟩ \\  & =4, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(1)\cdot a(1)}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

$$

Question 13
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨2t,t,t3⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=1s.

a
 33ms−2
b
 93ms−2
c
 3ms−2
d
 36ms−2
e
 26ms−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at t=1, as follows: v=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(t),ddt(t3)⟩=⟨2,1,3t2⟩v(1)=⟨2,1,3(1)2⟩=⟨2,1,3⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at t=1: a=⟨ddt(2),ddt(1),ddt(3t2)⟩=⟨0,0,6t⟩a(1)=⟨0,0,6(1)⟩=⟨0,0,6⟩.

Then, we compute v(1)⋅a(1) and ||v(1)||:

v(1)⋅a(1)=⟨2,1,3⟩⋅⟨0,0,6⟩=18||v(1)||=(2)2+12+32=12=23

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at t=1, and we get aT=v(1)⋅a(1)||v(1)||=1823=33.

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is 33ms−2.

q-97763.name: Question 14
q-97763.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\pi \,\text{s}.$
q-97763.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=\pi ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,1⟩, \\ v(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩, \\ a(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )$ and $||v(\pi )||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi ) & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =0, \\ ||v(\pi )|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )}{||v(\pi )||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $0\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

q-97767.name: Question 15
q-97767.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-t{e}^{t},\,2t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0\,\text{s}.$
q-97767.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(t+1){e}^{t},\,2⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-(0+1){e}^{0},\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-(t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(t+2){e}^{t},\,0⟩, \\ a(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-(0+2){e}^{0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(0)\cdot a(0)$ and $||v(0)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & =3, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

q-97767.html:
Question 15
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨et,−tet,2t⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=0s.

a
64ms−2
b
4ms−2
c
62ms−2
d
3ms−2
e
6ms−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at t=0, as follows: v=⟨ddt(et),ddt(−tet),ddt(2t)⟩=⟨et,−(t+1)et,2⟩,v(0)=⟨e0,−(0+1)e0,2⟩=⟨1,−1,2⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at t=0: a=⟨ddt(et),ddt(−(t+1)et),ddt(2)⟩=⟨et,−(t+2)et,0⟩,a(0)=⟨e0,−(0+2)e0,0⟩=⟨1,−2,0⟩

Then, we compute v(0)⋅a(0) and ||v(0)||:

v(0)⋅a(0)=⟨1,−1,2⟩⋅⟨1,−2,0⟩=3,||v(0)||=(1)2+(−1)2+(2)2=6

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at t=0, and we get aT=v(0)⋅a(0)||v(0)||=36=62.

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is 62ms−2.
